newsitem.title: USA: Arafat committed to restoring security - Albright.
newsitem.headline: Arafat committed to restoring security - Albright.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat committed himself to ensuring Israel's security after Wednesday's bombing in a Jerusalem market, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said.
Flying home from Asia, Albright called Arafat from her U.S. Air Force jet and was told "he was committed to restoring a secure atmosphere."
Fourteen people were kiled and more than 150 wounded in Wednesday's attack by two Arab suicide bombers.

Arafat "said to me he condemned the act and that he was meeting with his security officials and that they were doing everything they could to make sure the security situation is restored," Albright said.

She said she also called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. "We talked about the importance of returning to the peace process and I urged him to do so and he said he understood the importance of returning to the peace process... He did say he would (return to the process)."

Albright said she expected to speak again to both leaders once she was on the ground in Honolulu. She had planned to stay overnight after her trip to Asia but cut short the stay because of the bombing. She will be in Hawaii about 15 hours -- as long as Air Force regulations require for the pilots to rest.
